title: WordPress Launches AI-Powered Security Review to Block Malicious Plugin Updates
content_md: WordPress has introduced an automated, AI-powered security review process for every plugin release, aiming to stop vulnerable or malicious updates before delivering them to millions of websites through the platform’s update infrastructure. The new control analyzes plugin releases before they become available through the WordPress.org update API, including updates installed directly from the WordPress dashboard. Releases identified as posing a potentially high security risk will now be blocked automatically rather than relying on manual intervention by the Plugins Team. WordPress Launches AI-Powered Security Review The initiative addresses a longstanding supply-chain security gap in the WordPress ecosystem. While new plugins receive an initial review before entering the official directory, developers can continuously ship later updates. A plugin that is secure at publication can subsequently introduce a coding flaw, a compromised dependency, or deliberately implanted malicious functionality. WordPress said the capability builds on a cooldown mechanism introduced on June 5 for plugin and theme releases. WordPress holds every release before distribution through the update API; the current cooldown window is six hours. The delay gives automated systems time to inspect code changes before they reach active installations.
